input_context.user_message: One offer is AUD 70,000 plus super and another is AUD 40 per hour casual. Compare them as 70,000 versus 40 and tell me which pays more.

ui.purpose: Show the structural differences between salaried full-time and hourly casual pay components before comparison.
ui.prompt: Here is how the two pay structures break down. To compare them accurately, weekly hours and leave/loading factors need to be aligned.

rows.label: Superannuation
cells: Included or on top depends on award/contract

rows.label: Employment Basis
cells: Casual (typically includes 25% loading, no paid leave)

ui.purpose: Capture expected weekly hours for the casual role to normalise annualised earnings.
ui.prompt: How many hours per week do you expect to work in the casual role?

options.label: Full-time equivalent (38 hrs/week)
options.detail: At 38 hrs/week across ~52 weeks, casual earnings equal approx AUD 79,040 (without paid leave).

options.label: Substantial hours (~30 hrs/week)
options.detail: At 30 hrs/week across ~52 weeks, casual earnings equal approx AUD 62,400.

options.label: Part-time (~20 hrs/week)
options.detail: At 20 hrs/week across ~52 weeks, casual earnings equal approx AUD 41,600.

options.label: Unsure / Variable roster
options.detail: Hours are not guaranteed week to week.

derived_signals.signal: Offer A specifies annual salary of AUD 70,000 plus superannuation
Offer B specifies hourly casual rate of AUD 40 per hour
Direct raw comparison of 70,000 vs 40 is invalid without standardising period and hours basis
derived_signals.basis: FTE salaried ongoing pay includes paid annual/personal leave; casual hourly rate includes casual loading in lieu of paid leave and lacks guaranteed hours.

unknowns: Expected weekly hours and roster regularity for the AUD 40/hr casual role
Whether Offer B superannuation is inclusive or additional to the $40/hr rate
Jurisdiction / relevant Modern Award or Enterprise Agreement classification for either offer
Unpaid leave/time-off allowance assumptions for the casual role across a full year

pay_employment_profile.employment_type: Mixed: Salaried FTE vs Casual Hourly

comparability_notes.label: Basis Normalisation
comparability_notes.detail: An annual salary of $70,000 at 38 hrs/week equates to approx $35.42/hr base plus 4 weeks paid leave and personal leave. A casual rate of $40/hr includes a ~25% casual loading in lieu of paid leave (effective base ~$32/hr equivalent).

unknowns.label: Casual Hours
unknowns.detail: Total gross pay for the casual role depends entirely on rostered hours worked per week.

result.summary: Stated pay components received for both offers. Direct comparison requires standardising the casual role's expected weekly hours and factoring in leave entitlements.

readiness.name: Pay-and-Employment Evidence Readiness

dimensions.name: Pay Component Specificity
dimensions.reason: Base figures are provided (AUD 70k vs AUD 40/hr), but casual super status and award minimums are unverified.

dimensions.name: Hours & Employment Basis
dimensions.reason: Casual weekly hours and roster stability are unknown, preventing a like-for-like gross annual comparison.

dimensions.name: Legal / Award Verification
dimensions.reason: Neither role has a verified modern award, classification, or contract terms.

blockers: Casual weekly hours must be defined to establish comparable earnings.
Award classification and super treatment for the casual rate are unconfirmed.

next_actions.label: Specify casual hours to compare total gross earnings

handoff.summary: Received AUD 70,000 + super (annual/ongoing) and AUD 40/hr (casual). Requested expected weekly casual hours to normalise and compare pay structures accurately.

result.summary: Identified structural differences between $70k annual FTE and $40/hr casual. Awaiting weekly hours assumption to complete normalisation.

evidence_and_unknowns: Unknown: whether $40/hr is inclusive of super
handoff.recommended_next_action: Select expected casual hours to run normalised earnings comparison.
